subject: Performance validation workshop — scheduling & testplan review
messages:
From: Tom Li <tom.li@datahaven.ai>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-28T16:05:00-07:00
Subject: Request: performance validation workshop and test-plan review

Hi Grace,

Thanks for the demo last week — the team here at DataHaven wants to move to a short, hands-on performance validation session before we sign the Dedicated capacity commitment. High level asks: a joint workshop to walk through our prompt set, routing rules, and a focused load test to validate throughput + latency SLOs against our peak traffic.

Target metrics we care about:
- Throughput: sustain ~500 requests/minute (expected avg prompt length ~180 tokens)
- Latency SLO: 95th percentile <= 300 ms for generation (streaming ok)
- Steady-state run: 45–60 min with KV cache warm-up and a short ramp period

Can your team run a 90-minute workshop where: 1) we review the prompt set and routing fallbacks, 2) Redwood runs the load harness and we observe metrics, and 3) we capture next-step runbook items? Prefer week of Nov 1.

I'll attach a small sample of prompts and a list of the routes we plan to use. If you need any pre-reads, let me know.

Thanks,
Tom
Head of ML Ops
DataHaven

Attachments: sample_prompts.csv (sample prompts + expected labels)

From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
To: Tom Li <tom.li@datahaven.ai>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-29T09:18:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: performance validation workshop and test-plan review

Tom — thanks for the clear ask. We'd be happy to run that session and the load validation. Proposed plan:

- 30 min: prompt + routing review (we'll highlight caching and batching considerations)
- 50 min: load run (15 min ramp / 30 min steady / 5 min cool-down)
- 10 min: debrief + next steps and runbook action items

Attendees from our side: Aditya (SE) and Neha (AM). Please confirm the week of Nov 1 availability; we have the following open slots (PST):
- Tue Nov 3: 10:00–11:30
- Wed Nov 4: 14:00–15:30
- Thu Nov 5: 09:00–10:30

Before the run please share: full prompt CSV, routing map, and a target sequence-length distribution if possible. I attached an internal runbook skeleton (redwood-runbook-v0.2.pdf) and a short checklist that we'll follow.

Notes: for a clean throughput run we'll want control over the KV-cache warm-up (we typically recommend a 10–15 minute warm-up at low QPS) and an agreed set of fallback models in case we hit capacity limits.

Cheers,
Grace O'Connor
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood-runbook-v0.2.pdf

From: Tom Li <tom.li@datahaven.ai>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
Cc: DataHaven Ops <ops@datahaven.ai>
Date: 2026-10-30T08:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: performance validation workshop and test-plan review

Grace — thanks. Wed Nov 4 at 14:00 PST works best for the team. I've attached the full prompt set and a quick routing map. A couple clarifications:

- Sequence-length distro: 60% short (<=120 tokens), 30% mid (121–300), 10% long (>300)
- We'll want to exercise two routes: "priority" (premium users) and "bulk" (batched low-priority).
- We can provide a small VM that will run the client harness and push requests to your endpoint; will that suffice?

Attached: sample_prompts.csv (full), routing_map.pdf

Tom

Attachments: sample_prompts.csv

From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>, Tom Li <tom.li@datahaven.ai>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-01T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: performance validation workshop and test-plan review

Looping in some technical details from my side so we have a consistent run. Checklist / ask from Redwood SE:

- Harness: we'll use the mini-run harness (attached config) with configurable ramp and steady windows. Default run: 15m ramp -> 40m steady -> 5m cooldown.
- Batch/quantization: we'll test with your usual models; please confirm whether you want quantized variants during the run or strictly FP16. If unsure, we'll do FP16 first then a second shorter run with quantization.
- KV cache warm-up: plan for two warm-up phases — a short 10m prefix-warm and a 20m medium ramp prior to the steady window for the priority route.
- Metrics: we'll emit per-route KPIs (RPS, p50/p95 latency, GPU util, token burn). We'll stream the dashboard to the meeting.

Attached: load_harness_config.json (run parameters + seed traffic script)

If Wed Nov 4 14:00 PST is confirmed, I'll create the runbook entry in JIRA SUP-4782 and share a workspace link.

Thanks — Aditya
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachments: load_harness_config.json

From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
To: Tom Li <tom.li@datahaven.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-02T10:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: performance validation workshop and test-plan review

Confirmed: Wed Nov 4, 2026 — 14:00–15:30 PST. Calendar invite sent to attendees and ops VM. Summary of prep items (please drop files in the shared drive link below before EOD Nov 3):

- DataHaven: final prompt CSV, routing map, client-harness credentials (ops VM)
- Redwood: runbook (we'll use redwood-runbook-v0.2 as the base), load harness config, dashboard link
- Agreed run: 15m ramp / 30m steady / 5m cool-down; priority route gets explicit cache warm-up as noted.

Links: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-example-runbook
JIRA: SUP-4782

We'll also capture action items during the session for the Dedicated capacity checklist (SLA gating + fallbacks). Looking forward — see you Wed.

Best,
Grace O'Connor
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
Phone: +1 (415) 555-0142

Calendar: invite attached (Performance validation workshop — Redwood x DataHaven)
